description:
A function stored in a map or struct field cannot be called after it is read back. The compiler panics on interp and run; Elixir prints 1001.

Smallest repro:

    def sample(n), do: %{step: fn x -> x + n end}

    def main() do
      s = sample(1)
      dbg(s.step.(1000))
    end

Same failure with a struct (`defstruct [:step]`, `%Sample{step: fn x -> x + n end}`), whether called as `s.step.(1000)` or through `f = s.step; f.(1000)`, and whether the read is in the same function or a callee.

Panic: src/compiler2/jobs/transport.rs:913 "closure callee layout TransportLayout { structural: ShapeId(12), carrier: Absent } carries neither the captures of the 1 target(s) its callsite names nor one public word".

What is known:
- Present on develop (seen at cca160808 and again on the tip based on 8bf8775ae), so it predates the fz-3sy typed-path work.
- The same closure carried in a tuple and destructured works: `{:ok, f} = sample(1); f.(1000)` prints 1001 on run.
- The callee value read from the field has an Absent carrier: the field read is not demanding the closure as a callable word, while the callsite still names its one target.
- GH #302 is a different closure defect; no board ticket covers this.

Not yet known: whether the miss is in the demand the field read places on the stored closure, or in the transport of a closure through a map/struct field. Investigate before building; proposal page first.

Done when: the three shapes above (map field, struct field direct, struct field via a local) print 1001 on interp, run and build against the Elixir oracle, and fixture 00855 can call the function from its struct field directly instead of carrying it inside a tuple.
title: Calling a closure read from a map or struct field panics the compiler
